correctness.rationale: Treat the channels as an indexed frame, so duplicate vectors when b_j=2 retain separate labels. The identity C²+D²=I gives a Parseval analysis map. For any bounded U=(U_0,U_1), including those mixing coordinates, the Nth coordinate of CU_0e_N+DU_1e_N=e_N forces the Nth coordinate of U_1e_N to equal d_N^−1 when P_NU_0=0. Thus the squared norm is at least b_N. Using second-channel d_j^−1 only on j≤N and the Parseval dual on the tail achieves this bound by orthogonality and monotonicity, including plateaus. Q_NT has minimum modulus d_N; Q_∞T=(0,D) is injective but not bounded below. D has dense nonclosed range, and the exact sum of subspaces is H⊕D(H); no bounded right inverse for D exists. For every bounded dual, U_0−I=(I−C)U_0−DU_1 is compact, so U_0e_j−e_j tends to zero in norm and ||U_0||≥1. T attains equality; the chosen finite optimizers have defects C(I−P_N) of norm one converging strongly to zero. These conclusions hold over the reals or complexes. The frozen rational checker was read, not executed; its selected finite diagonal diagnostics cannot establish the all-operator infimum or any infinite conclusion.

value.rationale: For the natural question of taking a growing set of vanishing coefficient moments, mere infeasibility at the limit would only demonstrate the familiar positive-angle obstruction. The arbitrary exact costs, despite a perfect reference Parseval bound, rule out every a priori growth restriction on finite optimal conditioning in this class. The exact gap of one shows why strong decay of defects on inputs does not yield a uniform approximate constrained dual. This is useful as a sharp boundary example, not a general classification of frames.
